outline.description: Motivation behind moving away from fixed-token vocabularies, challenges of byte-level modeling, and an overview of the Byte Latent Transformer (BLT) contributions.
subtopics: Limitations of tokenization: domain bias, noise sensitivity, multilingual inequity
Why bytes? Flexibility and robustness
Historical attempts at byte‑level LLMs and their scaling bottlenecks
Key ideas of BLT: dynamic patching, latent transformer, compute allocation
Summary of contributions and roadmap of the textbook

outline.chapter_title: Fundamentals of Patching – From Bytes to Variable‑Size Units
outline.description: Formal definition of patches, how they differ from tokens, and detailed discussion of the three patching strategies used in BLT.
subtopics: Notation: sequences of bytes \(x_i\), patches \(p_j\), and the patching function \(f_p\)
Metrics influencing patch cost: average patch size and FLOP impact
Static (strided) patching – implementation and drawbacks
Space patching – heuristic based on whitespace and its linguistic intuition
Entropy‑based dynamic patching – training a small byte LM, computing next‑byte entropy, thresholding strategies (global vs monotonic)
Incremental vs non‑incremental patching; why BPE fails the incremental property
Comparison table: tokenization vs each patching method

outline.chapter_title: Architecture of the Byte Latent Transformer
outline.description: Detailed walk‑through of BLT’s three‑module design: local encoder, global latent transformer, and local decoder, including all key components such as cross‑attention and hash n‑gram embeddings.
subtopics: High‑level block diagram and data flow during training & inference
Global Latent Transformer: layer count, block‑causal attention, role in FLOP budget
Local Encoder:
- Byte embedding matrix (size 256 × h_E)
- Hash n‑gram embeddings (construction, rolling polynomial hash, dimensionality choices)
- Encoder transformer layers with local block‑causal windows
- Cross‑attention design (Perceiver style) for pooling bytes into patch queries
- Initialization of queries (max‑pool vs learned)
- Positional encoding choices (none vs RoPE) and rationale
Local Decoder:
- Symmetric cross‑attention (bytes query, patches key/value)
- Decoder transformer layers and output projection to 256‑byte vocab
- Training objective: byte‑level cross‑entropy → Bits‑Per‑Byte metric
- Interaction between encoder/decoder hidden states

outline.description: How BLT is pretrained, the datasets used, entropy model training, and practical details for maintaining comparable FLOP budgets.
subtopics: Pretraining corpora: Llama‑2 mix vs BLT‑1T dataset; cleaning & filtering steps

Determining entropy thresholds to achieve target average patch size
Batch composition under variable patch counts; padding & truncation strategy
Maintaining constant byte context length across models (8 k vs 16 k bytes)
Optimizer settings, learning rate schedule, weight decay & gradient clipping
FLOP accounting methodology (forward + backward) for each module

outline.description: Empirical scaling experiments that compare compute‑optimal BLT models with tokenizers across parameter regimes and FLOP budgets.

Impact of average patch size on inference FLOPs; trade‑off analysis

"Fixed inference FLOP" scaling study – how larger patches enable bigger models under a static budget

outline.description: Performance comparison of BLT variants with tokenized baselines on standard benchmarks covering reasoning, coding, classification and multilingual translation.
